A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AuroraCap, VDC and VDCscore. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable despite reformatting, renumbering and supplementary additions.

before.justification: v1 reports original AuroraCap captioning and question-answering results, token-merging and training ablations, and comparisons with human Elo judgments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds long-video evaluations and further analyses of the proposed evaluation metric.

M1.justification: Section S3 adds an evaluated VDCscore variant that uses ROUGE for final answer matching instead of LLM judgment. AuroraCap's architecture, frame-wise token merging, three-stage training and default VDCscore procedure remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Section S2 adds actual evaluation on MovieChat-1K and EgoSchema, substantially extending coverage to long-form video understanding. MovieChat-1K was only discussed as related work in v1. Existing training datasets, captioning benchmarks and other evaluations are retained.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds InstructBLIP-7B and InstructBLIP-13B. New long-video comparisons include previously unevaluated comparators such as TimeChat, mPLUG-Owl and VideoLLAMA2, while Section S9 adds CLIP similarity as a metric comparator. Existing principal comparison sets are retained.

E3.justification: Supplementary evaluations introduce ROUGE answer matching, CLIP scoring, and controls using 5 and 10 QA pairs alongside the existing 20-pair setup. New MovieChat-1K results distinguish breakpoint and global evaluation. Previously reported training hyperparameters, decoding settings and benchmark sample counts remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Sections S2, S3 and S9 substantially expand validation through an EgoSchema token-retention ablation, alternative answer-matching analysis, CLIP-versus-human correlation, and QA-count sensitivity. These examine long-sequence robustness and metric design choices beyond v1's retained token-merging, slowfast, efficiency, training and backbone analyses.

E5.justification: No new repeated-run counts, seeds, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation procedures are reported. Added correlation plots follow the existing reporting approach. Elo parameters, including the reported 2,778 matches, are unchanged.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include AuroraCap's MovieChat-1K breakpoint/global scores of 52.6/59.7 and EgoSchema accuracy of 46.0, plus human correlations of 0.74 for ROUGE answer matching and 0.39 for CLIP. Added InstructBLIP-7B achieves 118.2 NoCaps CIDEr versus AuroraCap's retained 111.4. Existing AuroraCap main-table and appendix ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The token-size-adjusted attention equation and per-layer merging formula are unchanged; v1 Equation 2 becomes v2 Equation S1. No new mathematical assumptions, proofs or derivations accompany the additional empirical metric analyses.

C1.justification: The introduction reframes AuroraCap from a claimed state-of-the-art video captioning model to a video-understanding base model with improved captioning performance. The central claims concerning token efficiency, the VDC benchmark and VDCscore remain intact.

C2.justification: Section S1 newly argues that sparse frames and image-trained CLIP features make strong temporal merging undesirable. Section S9 suggests CLIP misses fine-grained caption errors and interprets additional QA pairs as improving robustness. Table 2 also qualifies the unusually low cited GPT-4V scores; existing OCR limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Sections S17-S18 supply previously omitted answer-extraction and correctness-evaluation prompts. v2 also specifies the GPT-4o usage period and explains randomized, model-blinded Elo comparisons in S15. Direct code/model access information is added, while resource wording changes from already available to future release; actual availability cannot be established from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to EgoSchema, OmniCorpus and MM-Ego. Section S1 expands positioning against Chat-UniVi's temporal token handling and distinguishes VDCscore evaluation from LLaVA-Hound-DPO's preference-data construction. Most related-work coverage is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and the main section sequence remain intact. Changes include localized copyediting, numeric citation style, revised author/header information, expanded supplementary explanations, and limited reordering within the ablation discussion. The appendices are reorganized from lettered sections into S1-S18.

P2.justification: Document-wide retypesetting changes page geometry, title and abstract styling, headers, table headings, and figure/table sizing and placement. New displays include Figures S1-S4, Figure S15 and Table S1. Existing visualizations and case-study images are largely retained and relocated.

improvement.justification: The new long-video and metric analyses broaden evidential support, while the missing evaluation prompts and clearer Elo procedure improve reproducibility. The gain is limited by sparse settings for the new long-video experiments and misleading best-score bolding in Table 2, which overlooks the added InstructBLIP NoCaps results. Overall, the additions provide a useful incremental improvement.
